Stage 1 admits the performance because its specific musical architecture puts Sakurai's electric-bass fusion language against Oki's flamenco guitar, with flute and percussion completing a deliberately cross-genre quartet and a program spanning the leaders' originals and flamenco repertoire. Stage 2 assigns A+: this is actively worth making room for within a Tokyo stay because the unusual bass/flamenco pairing and lineup create a distinct live proposition. events.factual_description: EBISU JAM 2026 and Jin Oki's official site list Tetsuo Sakurai with Jin Oki featuring Rie Akagi and Kan at The Garden Hall in Ebisu on Friday, October 9, 2026. Doors are at 17:45 and the performance starts at 18:30. The announced lineup is Sakurai on bass, Oki on guitar, Akagi on flute, and Kan on percussion. Jin Oki's event page describes the billing as a long-awaited collaboration and says the program will range from original pieces by Sakurai and Oki to flamenco numbers. The official ticket price is ¥8,800 for a reserved seat, with a separate drink charge. Sakurai's official schedule independently confirms the same date, venue, and four-person lineup.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is the collision of instrumental languages. Sakurai brings the attack, harmonic mobility and groove of Japanese electric-bass fusion; Oki answers with flamenco guitar, while Rie Akagi's flute and Kan's percussion keep the quartet from settling into a standard fusion-band shape. The announced program moves between the two leaders' originals and flamenco material, so this is a real cross-genre working session rather than a guest spot pasted onto somebody else's set. If bass, guitar and rhythmic dialogue are part of the Tokyo thread, actively make room for it.
en.trip_verdict: If October 9 falls inside a Tokyo stay, I would build the Ebisu evening around this performance. The lineup is unusual enough to justify crossing the city, but I would not reshape an entire Japan itinerary solely around it; the special collaboration is strong without needing artificial travel urgency.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho está en el choque de lenguajes instrumentales. Sakurai trae el ataque, la movilidad armónica y el groove de la fusión japonesa de bajo eléctrico; Oki responde desde la guitarra flamenca, mientras la flauta de Rie Akagi y la percusión de Kan evitan que el cuarteto termine sonando como una banda de fusión convencional. El programa anunciado se mueve entre originales de los dos líderes y repertorio flamenco, así que esto funciona como una sesión de cruce real y no como un invitado pegado al set de otro músico. Si el hilo de Tokio trae bajo, guitarra y conversación rítmica, sí le haría espacio activamente.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 9 de octubre cae dentro de una estancia en Tokio, armaría la noche de Ebisu alrededor de esta función. La formación es suficientemente inusual para justificar cruzar la ciudad, pero no reordenaría todo un itinerario por Japón únicamente por ella; la colaboración especial ya es fuerte sin fabricar urgencia de viaje.
